title: Ordinary tensor homology for modules over a constant field quotient
statement: Let T be a scheme and A a commutative ring. On the original small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], write R_A for the constant commutative ring sheaf and use its intrinsic module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let r in A generate a maximal ideal, put k=A/(r), and let N be the unit module of the constant ring sheaf R_k, restricted to R_A by the canonical quotient map (the coefficient module used in [def-weil-derived-tensor]). Let P be any possibly unbounded cochain complex of R_A-modules and let M be any R_A-module sheaf annihilated by the canonical constant sections of r. For every integer i, if H^i of the ordinary termwise sheaf tensor P tensor N is zero, then H^i of P tensor M is zero. Tensor is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. No K-flatness, nilpotence, constructibility or interval hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 03CY, 0GMW and 03EI; original residue-test proof step 3

proof.text: Restrict scalar actions along the constant-presheaf sheafification unit. Because r kills M, the restriction is a presheaf of modules over the field k=A/(r), with compatible restriction maps. Module sheafification over the constant presheaf k recovers its underlying abelian sheaf. Form the analogous k-presheaf complex presenting C=P tensor_A N.

Use tensor/sheafification comparison in the site object and Hom universes to identify sheafified presheaf tensors with intrinsic sheaf tensors. Work over the constant presheaf field k, never over a section ring of its sheafification.

Apply the existing constant-field tensor/cohomology theorem to the field-module complex C and the factored module M. It gives H^i(C tensor_k M) isomorphic to H^i(C) tensor_k M. Its sectionwise proof uses split vector-space sequences, with the canonical map [z] tensor m -> [z tensor m], followed by exact sheafification; no vanishing of presheaf section homology is assumed. The right side is zero by the given sheaf homology vanishing, after the comparisons of step 2.

The balanced maps (p tensor t) tensor m -> p tensor (t m) and p tensor m -> (p tensor 1) tensor m are inverse and commute with restrictions and differentials. After sheafification they identify C tensor_k M with P tensor_A M. Transport the vanishing from step 3 through this isomorphism. The zero module and zero complex, all integer degrees, and the empty scheme are included.

proof_origin.place: G3 isolates precisely the ordinary field-module calculation of proof step 3, not a new Tor-amplitude test

lean.statement:
theorem proEtale_residue_module_tensor_homology
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (r : A)
    (hr : (Ideal.span {r}).IsMaximal)
    (P : CochainComplex (proEtaleRingModules T (proEtaleConstantRing T A)) ℤ)
    (M : proEtaleRingModules T (proEtaleConstantRing T A))
    (hM : ∀ (U : T.ProEtᵒᵖ) (x : M.val.obj U),
      (toSheafify (ProEt.topology T)
        ((Functor.const T.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)))).app U
          (ULift.up r) • x = 0)
    (i : ℤ) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory (proEtaleConstantRing T A)
    let B := A ⧸ Ideal.span {r}
    let RB := proEtaleConstantRing T B
    let SB := (sheafCompose (ProEt.topology T) (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj RB
    let α := (sheafCompose (ProEt.topology T) (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).map
      ((constantSheaf (ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (RingHom.ulift (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {r})))))
    let N := (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u + 1} α).obj (SheafOfModules.unit SB)
    IsZero ((((tensorRight N).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P).homology i) →
    IsZero ((((tensorRight M).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P).homology i)
